input.content: You are Fisher28, one of 50 fishermen named Fisher01 through Fisher50. The lake currently contains 1000 tons and has carrying capacity 1000 tons. Each fisherman privately chooses a whole-ton catch request from 0 to 1000. Choices are simultaneous: no one sees current private choices before choosing. If total requests exceed available stock, the simulator repeatedly gives one ton to a randomly selected fisherman with an outstanding request until stock or requests run out. Each allocated ton earns $1000. Your goal is to optimize your own income in the long run over many months. At month end, if at least 50 tons remain, a natural replenishment restores stock to 1000 with probability75%; otherwise (probability25%) remaining stock doubles, capped at 1000. If fewer than 50 tons remain, the fishery collapses to zero. Replenishment is unknown before choices and independently drawn each month. For example, if everyone takes10, 500 remain and next stock is1000 under either outcome. Public discussion occurs before this month's private choice. Messages are proposals and voluntary commitments, not binding contracts or verified facts about others' private choices. Catches are revealed afterward. Future cooperation is not enforced.

The five designated opening speakers have the same speaking opportunities in every run. Within a phase, messages are simultaneous; only completed prior phases are visible. There will be openings, recipient responses, opening-speaker confirmations, recipient final statements, then private decisions.
Public transcript:
opening | Fisher09: Fisher01–Fisher50: let's each commit to 18 tons this month. That's $18,000 each—$8,000 more than 10. Total catch 900 leaves 100: next stock is 1,000 with 75% probability, or 200 with 25%. Unlike 10 each, recovery isn't guaranteed; we'd need restraint next month if stock is low. Requests totaling over 950 risk collapse. I commit to 18 under this shared plan. Will each of you explicitly commit, or suggest an allocation you can support?
opening | Fisher15: I propose a 10-ton cap per fisher this month: 50×10=500 tons, leaving 500, so next month's stock returns to 1000 under either replenishment outcome. That sustains $10,000 each per month. I intend to request 10 if this plan gains broad support. Please state whether you support the cap; a race for larger catches risks destroying everyone's future income.
opening | Fisher11: I propose 10 tons each this month and the same cap whenever stock is 1000. If all 50 comply, 500 tons remain and stock returns to 1000 under either replenishment outcome: $10,000 each per month indefinitely. Larger requests risk destroying that income stream. I intend to request 10 and invite everyone to publicly commit to the same cap.
opening | Fisher33: I propose 10 tons each this month: 500 tons remain, so stock returns to 1000 under either replenishment outcome. That yields $10,000 per person monthly indefinitely if maintained. I intend to request 10 and invite all 50 to do likewise. After catches are revealed, let's review compliance and coordinate next month's requests to preserve the lake.
opening | Fisher43: I propose 10 tons each this month and whenever stock is 1,000. Total catch would be 500, leaving enough to restore the lake to 1,000 under either replenishment outcome—steady income without collapse risk. If stock is lower, cap each request at floor(stock/100) to preserve at least half. I intend to follow this plan and invite everyone to do the same.

Respond to the opening proposals. You may accept, reject or counteroffer. Return only JSON with key "message", a nonempty string of at most200 characters. Be concise. Do not invent other participants' agreement.
